Projects

Projections

An essay that teaches Fourier transforms by locking you in an escape room with a signal, a keypad and a chatbot that will only explain things twice. A paper that squeezes momentum tensors with a cosine transform sent me off to learn the transform properly, which took about two months. The maths is typeset with KaTeX, and the first figure is only the vector (3, 7) split into its two coordinates. [draft]

Built with: HTML, CSS, KaTeX

Eliza

I wrote a small Python class for the capital asset pricing model. Give it a stock and an index, and it downloads the prices, regresses one on the other, and reports the beta, the alpha, and how much of the stock's volatility is the market's and how much is its own. A second method turns those into dollars of risk. I haven't written the last two methods yet, and every new instance prints a large green ASCII banner. [draft]

Built with: Python, pandas, statsmodels, yfinance

Code

Ada

I wrote a bot that posts videos from a Google Drive folder to Instagram as Reels, one at a time, with at least a minute between uploads. Which videos have already gone out is kept in a Supabase table instead of a local file, so the Docker container can be restarted without posting anything twice. My README admits it may break Instagram's terms of service, so read it as an exercise in plumbing. [draft]

Built with: Python, Docker, Supabase, Google Drive API, instagrapi

Code

Stryder

My question was whether a small neural network can learn to undo a messy cipher from examples alone. Each letter of a word is encrypted by a randomly chosen scheme out of five (shift, XOR, substitution, Base64 and bit reversal), and an LSTM encoder and decoder learns to turn the ciphertext back into the word. The detail that makes it learnable is the seed: every word's randomness comes from one of only twenty seeds, which gives the network some structure to find. In the notebook, the training loss falls from 1.76 to 0.004 over 100 epochs. [draft]

Built with: Python, PyTorch, Weights & Biases

Fun

Ellie

The New York Times emails a daily briefing, and the photographs in it are good enough that I wanted to keep them. Ellie reads those emails through the Gmail API, pulls out every image larger than 500 by 500 pixels, and files them in a folder named after the day. It cannot yet handle multipart emails, which is on the to-do list. [draft]

Built with: Python, Gmail API, Beautiful Soup, Pillow

Code

Naive Discrete Fourier Transform

A Fourier transform written from scratch, to see if I could turn the maths on paper into code that recovers the frequencies hiding in a signal. The toy signal is five sine and cosine waves added together, and the code finds each one by multiplying by a complex exponential at that frequency and integrating. The strongest wave, at 7 Hz, has an amplitude of 100, which makes the other four look a bit sad. [draft]

Built with: Python, NumPy, Matplotlib
